restaurants.name: Holbox
restaurants.description: Gilberto Cetina Jr.'s Yucatecan seafood stall inside Mercado La Paloma. The ceviche, octopus tacos, and Baja-style fish are transcendent — this is some of the best seafood in LA at any price point.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin Bib Gourmand. Consistently on every best-of list in LA. Go early — it gets packed by noon.
restaurants.address: 3655 S Grand Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90007

restaurants.name: Burritos La Palma
restaurants.description: Legendary flour tortillas made fresh to order, wrapped around braised meats and chile rellenos. The birria burrito is a religious experience. Worth the drive to OC.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin Bib Gourmand. The tortillas alone are worth the pilgrimage.

restaurants.name: Jitlada
restaurants.description: Jazz Singsanong's legendary Southern Thai restaurant in a strip mall. The crying tiger beef, morning glory, and Southern Thai curries are searingly authentic. Jonathan Gold's favorite.
restaurants.whyHot: Jonathan Gold championed this place for years. Still unmatched for Southern Thai heat.
restaurants.address: 5233 W Sunset Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90027

restaurants.name: Mariscos Jalisco
restaurants.description: Raul Ortega's famous truck serving the crispiest shrimp tacos in LA. The tacos dorados de camaron are legendary — a deep-fried corn tortilla packed with shrimp, topped with avocado and salsa.
restaurants.whyHot: The shrimp taco that launched a thousand imitators. Cash only, outdoor seating.
restaurants.address: 3040 E Olympic Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90023

restaurants.name: Howlin' Ray's
restaurants.description: Johnny Ray Zone's Nashville hot chicken, the dish that changed LA's relationship with spicy fried chicken forever. The Howlin' heat level is not for the faint of heart.
restaurants.whyHot: The line is shorter at the new Pasadena location. Still the gold standard for hot chicken in LA.

restaurants.name: Sapp Coffee Shop
restaurants.description: The jade noodle soup and boat noodles at this unassuming Thai Town institution are the stuff of LA food legend. Jonathan Gold gave it a perfect review. Cash only.
restaurants.whyHot: A Jonathan Gold essential. Boat noodles are the move.

restaurants.name: Sonoratown
restaurants.description: Hand-stretched Sonoran flour tortillas filled with carne asada, chivichanga, and caramelo (cheese-crusted quesadilla-taco hybrid). The tortillas are the star — paper-thin and impossibly good.
restaurants.whyHot: The caramelo changed the game. Multiple locations now but DTLA OG still hits different.

restaurants.name: Cheesesteaks by Matu
restaurants.description: Matsuhisa-trained chef making the best Philly cheesesteaks in LA from a pop-up window. Wagyu ribeye, housemade whiz, long hots. The crossover nobody expected.
restaurants.whyHot: Just added to Infatuation Hit List (3/4/2026). The fine-dining-to-cheesesteak pipeline is real.
restaurants.address: 5474 W Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90019

restaurants.name: Porridge + Puffs
restaurants.description: Minh Phan's congee shop with creative toppings and golden cream puffs. The XO congee with crab and the miso-brown-butter puff are small miracles. Tiny space, big flavors.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin Bib Gourmand. Minh Phan is one of LA's most original chefs.

restaurants.name: Guerrilla Tacos
restaurants.description: Wes Avila's boundary-pushing tacos that blend fine-dining technique with street food soul. Sweet potato taco with feta and fried corn, tuna tostada with uni. A new kind of LA taco.
restaurants.whyHot: From truck to brick-and-mortar, Wes Avila changed what a taco could be.

restaurants.name: Anajak Thai
restaurants.description: Justin Pichetrungsi transformed his parents' Thai restaurant into one of LA's most exciting dining experiences. Uni fried rice, crab fat noodles, and the freshest Thai seafood preparations in the city.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin star. Time Out just swapped out Spago for Anajak Thai in their Top 40. Reservations essential.

restaurants.name: Bestia
restaurants.description: Ori Menashe's industrial-chic Italian remains one of the hardest reservations in LA a decade later. The handmade pastas, roasted bone marrow, and charcoal-grilled meats are consistently extraordinary.
restaurants.whyHot: Still the reservation everyone wants. Late-night walk-ins at the bar are the move.

restaurants.name: Republique
restaurants.description: Walter and Margarita Manzke's all-day restaurant in the iconic Campanile building. Brunch is legendary (the fried chicken sandwich), dinner is polished French-Cal, and the pastries are among LA's finest.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin star. The brunch is still one of the best meals in LA at any price.
restaurants.address: 624 S La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90036

restaurants.name: Bavel
restaurants.description: Ori Menashe and Genevieve Gergis's Middle Eastern restaurant, the sibling to Bestia. The lamb neck shawarma, pita bread, and date-sweetened sticky toffee pudding are all-time great dishes.
restaurants.whyHot: Still one of the best restaurants in LA. The pita alone is worth the reservation.

restaurants.name: Yangban Society
restaurants.description: Katianna and John Hong's genre-defying Korean-American grocery-restaurant. The jjigae, the galbi, and the pastries represent a new wave of Korean-American cooking that doesn't flatten either tradition.
restaurants.whyHot: One of the most exciting openings of the 2020s. The grocery section is also incredible.

restaurants.name: Guelaguetza
restaurants.description: The Lopez family's Oaxacan institution. The mole negro alone is worth a lifetime of visits — seven types of chile, chocolate, and 30 ingredients slow-cooked to devastating complexity. Essential LA dining.
restaurants.whyHot: The definitive Oaxacan restaurant in the US. James Beard Award nominee.
restaurants.address: 3014 W Olympic Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90006

restaurants.name: Horses
restaurants.description: Will Aghajanian and Liz Johnson's Hollywood restaurant serves inventive Cal-Med cooking in a gorgeous room. The garlic bread is famous, the pastas are exceptional, and the wine list is adventurous.
restaurants.whyHot: One of LA's essential dinner spots. Walk-ins at the bar are possible but get there early.

restaurants.name: Kato
restaurants.description: Jon Yao's Michelin-starred tasting menu draws from Taiwanese tradition with California ingredients. The smoked tai-style sausage rice, Wagyu with XO, and pineapple cake finale are extraordinary.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin star. One of the most important restaurants in the Asian-American culinary movement.
restaurants.address: 11925 Santa Monica Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90025

restaurants.name: Sonmari
restaurants.description: Korean comfort food from a former Benu chef — soy-garlic wings, short rib ssam, and the silkiest tofu stew since Beverly Soon Tofu. A new Korean fine-casual that actually delivers on the hype.
restaurants.whyHot: Just added to Infatuation Hit List (3/4/2026). Book for 5:30pm or after 8pm for shortest wait.
restaurants.address: 1760 N Vermont Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90027

restaurants.name: Electric Bleu
restaurants.description: A moody French-Japanese fusion spot from the team behind Catch. Tuna tartare with yuzu, duck confit with miso glaze, and a late-night bar scene that rivals the dining room.
restaurants.whyHot: Resy March 2026 addition. The cocktail program is as much a draw as the food.

restaurants.name: Cuevita
restaurants.description: A mezcal-forward modern Mexican spot in Echo Park with a killer rooftop. Mole flights, blue corn tlayudas, and some of the most thoughtful agave cocktails in the city.
restaurants.whyHot: Resy March 2026 addition. The rooftop with the skyline view is worth the reservation alone.
restaurants.address: 1519 Echo Park Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90026

restaurants.name: Bess
restaurants.description: A lively Mediterranean restaurant from the team behind Mother Wolf. Wood-fired kebabs, handmade flatbreads, and a cocktail program built around pomegranate and rose. The ambiance is electric.
restaurants.whyHot: Resy March 2026 addition. The Mother Wolf team rarely misses — this is their most casual concept yet.

restaurants.name: Lapaba
restaurants.description: A modern Filipino restaurant bringing adobo, sinigang, and sisig to a sit-down Silver Lake setting. The lechon kawali with spiced vinegar is the star. Filipino food's long-overdue moment in LA.
restaurants.whyHot: Just added to Infatuation Hit List (3/4/2026). Filipino food finally getting the restaurant treatment it deserves.

restaurants.name: Majordomo
restaurants.description: David Chang's LA outpost — a cavernous, industrial-chic space where the Korean-American cooking is brilliant: the bo ssam for the table, the bing with short rib, and some of the best noodles in the city.
restaurants.whyHot: The short rib bing is one of the most iconic dishes in LA. Great for groups.

restaurants.name: Hippo
restaurants.description: Matthew Kang's plant-forward restaurant that makes vegetables genuinely exciting. The mushroom dumplings, roasted cabbage, and market-driven tasting menu prove that vegetable cooking can be as thrilling as any protein.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin star. A game-changer for vegetable-forward dining in LA.

restaurants.name: Ine
restaurants.description: A chic izakaya bringing Kyoto-style small plates to WeHo. Grilled maitake, handroll bar, and an exceptional sake list. The late-night omakase counter is the hidden gem.
restaurants.whyHot: Resy March 2026 addition. The izakaya format fills a real gap in WeHo's dining scene.
restaurants.address: 8905 Santa Monica Blvd, West Hollywood, CA 90069

restaurants.name: Petit Trois
restaurants.description: Ludo Lefebvre's no-reservations French bistro. The Big Mec burger, the omelette, and the steak frites are textbook — simple food executed at the highest level. No pretension, just skill.
restaurants.whyHot: The best French bistro food in LA. No reservations — first come, first served.

restaurants.name: Rustic Canyon
restaurants.description: Andy Doubrava and Jeremy Fox's market-driven Californian restaurant. The wood-fired vegetables, pristine seafood, and impeccable wine list make this a neighborhood restaurant that happens to be extraordinary.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin star. The platonic ideal of California cooking — seasonal, beautiful, honest.

restaurants.name: Destroyer
restaurants.description: Jordan Kahn's daytime counterpart to Vespertine. Every dish is a miniature artwork: smoked salmon with horseradish cream, granola with sorrel yogurt, and the fluffiest brioche in LA. Fine dining at breakfast prices.
restaurants.whyHot: Jordan Kahn making beautiful food accessible. The aesthetic alone is worth the visit.

restaurants.name: Hatch
restaurants.description: A yakitori counter experience with binchotan charcoal-grilled skewers and Japanese whisky. Every cut of the chicken is represented, nose-to-tail, grilled to perfection by chefs trained in Tokyo.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin-recommended. The best yakitori experience in LA, period.
restaurants.address: 3760 S La Cienega Blvd, Culver City, CA 90232

restaurants.name: Mother Wolf
restaurants.description: Evan Funke's Hollywood Roman pasta palace. The cacio e pepe is made tableside, the carbonara is textbook, and the amatriciana sings. A maximalist Italian experience in a stunning room.
restaurants.whyHot: The hardest reservation in Hollywood. The bar serves the full menu — insider move.

restaurants.name: Somni
restaurants.description: Aitor Zabala's 3-Michelin-star avant-garde Spanish tasting menu, hidden within the SLS Hotel. 20+ courses of molecular gastronomy that push the boundaries of what food can be. LA's most acclaimed restaurant.
restaurants.whyHot: Three Michelin stars — one of only two in LA. Book months in advance. A once-in-a-lifetime meal.
restaurants.address: 465 S La Cienega Blvd, Beverly Hills, CA 90211

restaurants.name: Providence
restaurants.description: Michael Cimarusti's 2-Michelin-star seafood restaurant, a cornerstone of fine dining in LA for two decades. The pristine seafood tasting menu — Santa Barbara uni, live spot prawn, market fish — is a celebration of the Pacific.
restaurants.whyHot: Two Michelin stars. The most consistently excellent fine dining restaurant in LA. The wine pairings are superb.

restaurants.name: Sushi Ginza Onodera
restaurants.description: Authentic Edomae sushi from a Ginza-trained itamae. Fish flown in from Tsukiji, rice seasoned with red vinegar, and the kind of minimalist precision that defines the highest level of sushi. The counter seats 8.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin star. The most authentic Tokyo-style omakase in LA. Counter only.
restaurants.address: 609 N La Cienega Blvd, West Hollywood, CA 90069

restaurants.name: Sushi Kaneyoshi
restaurants.description: Atsushi Kaneyoshi's intimate 10-seat omakase counter. Each piece of nigiri is a meditation — the rice is warm, the fish is pristine, and the progression tells a story. One of the finest sushi experiences in America.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin star. Atsushi-san's knife work is mesmerizing. Book two months out.

restaurants.name: n/naka
restaurants.description: Niki Nakayama's modern kaiseki is one of LA's most celebrated dining experiences. 13 courses rooted in Japanese seasonality but inflected with California — abalone, A5 Wagyu, and the iconic sashimi course.
restaurants.whyHot: Two Michelin stars. Featured on Chef's Table. Niki Nakayama is a national treasure.

restaurants.name: Hayato
restaurants.description: Brandon Go's traditional kaiseki in a spare, beautiful room inside the ROW DTLA complex. The most rigorously authentic Japanese multi-course meal in LA — each dish reflects the season with monastic precision.
restaurants.whyHot: Two Michelin stars. The most reverential dining experience in LA. Pure meditation.

restaurants.name: Mori Sushi
restaurants.description: Morihiro Onodera's long-running West LA sushi counter is a quiet masterclass. No theatrics, no molecular tricks — just impeccable fish, perfect rice, and decades of experience behind every piece.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin star. The most under-the-radar great sushi in LA. True connoisseur's choice.
restaurants.address: 11500 W Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90064

restaurants.name: Camphor
restaurants.description: Max Boonthanakit and Lijo George's modern French restaurant quickly became one of LA's finest. The sourdough bread service, the duck, and the mille-feuille are extraordinary. French technique with global influences.
restaurants.whyHot: Michelin star. The fastest ascent in recent LA dining history. The bread course alone is worth the price.

restaurants.name: RVR
restaurants.description: A newcomer on the fine dining scene — an intimate French tasting menu that channels the precision of Parisian haute cuisine with Santa Monica produce. Time Out just added it to their Top 40, replacing Spago.
restaurants.whyHot: Time Out swapped Spago for RVR in their March 2026 update. The new guard arrives.
